featured_reviews.name: anandhi krishnan
featured_reviews.review_text:
We attended an 80th Birthday celebration in the community hall in the premises. The hall is an A/c one, airy and with a look of spaciousness. It can accommodate about 320 people with chairs seating.

Provision is available for serving food on tables on another level hall with a capacity of about 200 people in one go.

The premises have been kept very clean and well maintained.

The hall housing Lord Balaji at the ground level is also airy and the idol is really looming and magnificent. One can sit and feel the presence of the Lord in the quiet surroundings.

Overall, it’s one of the most serene, clean, and well-managed temples in Mulund — a perfect place to sit quietly, pray, and feel deeply connected.

featured_reviews.name: Anoup Sukale
featured_reviews.review_text: जय संतोषी माँ. This post is not about notation as any religious structure can not and should not be noted and since the times that we live in are all about those stars, I caved. Rather it’s a feeble attempt of essaying the historicity of one of the oldest temples in Mulund. These are mere memories of some facts and other not so trustworthy factoids that I learnt growing up in the family of the first priest of this temple, my maternal grandfather. The first picture attached to this comment has to be one of the oldest pictures in existence of Shree Maa Santoshi. You can see this image at the very beginning of the Vijay Sharma’s movie « Jai Santoshi Maa » which released in the month of May 1975, becoming a huge box office success and earning 50 million rupees which was twenty times it’s production cost. The movie was dethroned only by the star studded « Sholay » which got an independence day release in August of the same year. Ancient grapevine says that the makers of the movie wanted to film the temple scenes in Mulund but were denied the rights to do so by the then temple authorities allowing only this picture to be shown on the big screen without any identification. Mulund existed well before the establishment of the temple and was occupied since the Mauryan Empire dating as back as the first century BCE which corresponds roughly to the excavation of the Canheri Caves. It was known then as Mulachind or Mulkund, which later digressed as Mulund during the East India Company. It is one of the first towns of Mumbai to be purposefully planned in 1922 with right angle grids connecting the town to the Mulund west train station. The Britishers built India’s first Railway line between Thane and Bori Bunder in 1853 having added the Mulund station later.  To the west of the planned town though was a highly forested area, with a few agglomerations of thawed houses or chawls as locally known, amidst the greenery of the comparatively recent Sanjay Gandhi National Park which was created in 1969 and is the only national park inside the city limits in India. Back in the day the tree line descended the gentle slopes of Yogi Hills to cease in front of the Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg, which already was a national highway with pharmaceutical and engineering companies scattered all along its sides. Some say that this temple albeit in its ancient smaller structure witnessed it all alongside the Balrajeshwar Mahadev temple closeby. One fact that I can be sure about is that this temple is younger than  the Balrajeshwar Mahadev temple, which was rebuilt in 1901 as per the temple’s official website. There used to be a small mosque in the middle of the highway right in front of the temple which had been relocated during the construction and enlargement of the highway. As a kid, I had also heard whispers that the idol of the Goddess was left without worship for a long time under the Fig tree that used to stand behind her for years. A few meters away from the place where She was unearthed following a vision of a local unidentified or long forgotten person, who found the idol and placed her under the tree. My grandfather took great pride to be at her service until he drew his last breath in her name. I receive माँ संतोषी’s images by WhatsApp every morning sent by my cousin who is one of the priests today succeeding my grandfather. Joined are the images taken this morning. One can clearly see the same eyes in comparison to the oldest picture in this post and also see the erosion of the lips and the black eye sockets of the goddess’s idol. I can not say what inspired me to write this comment on a public forum. I guess it has something to do with the fact that I can grow away from my land, but I shan’t be uprooted so long as She who is the goddess of satisfaction keeps me humble and proud of my belief in Her. Also, I think sharing what little anecdotes I know about Her and Her first devotee, my grandfather, somehow rekindled my nostalgia of an ideal childhood spent in the queen of suburbs of Mumbai, ruled by the Goddess of satiation and satisfaction.

featured_reviews.name: AJAY TIWARI
featured_reviews.review_text:
Balrajeshwar Mahadev Temple is one of the most peaceful and spiritually uplifting places in Mulund. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, this temple holds a special place in the hearts of local devotees. The temple is known for its serene environment, which offers a perfect escape from the busy city life of Mumbai. As you enter, you immediately feel a sense of calm and positivity.
The architecture of the temple is simple yet traditional, maintaining a strong spiritual vibe. The Shiva Lingam is beautifully placed, and during occasions like Mahashivratri, the temple becomes vibrant with भक्तों की भीड़ and devotional energy. The chanting of mantras and ringing of bells create a divine atmosphere that enhances the overall experience.
The temple परिसर is clean and well-maintained, making it comfortable for visitors of all ages. The staff and volunteers are helpful and ensure smooth darshan for everyone. It is also a great place for meditation and quiet reflection.
Overall, Balrajeshwar Mahadev Temple is not just a place of worship but a spiritual retreat where one can find peace, devotion, and inner strength. A must-visit for anyone in Mulund.

featured_reviews.name: Nikita Kotak
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Balrajeshwar Mandir in Mulund is a truly peaceful and divine place to visit. The temple is beautifully maintained, with a calm and spiritual atmosphere that instantly brings positivity and peace of mind. The architecture is simple yet elegant, and the idol of Lord Shiva is mesmerizing.

It’s a perfect spot for daily darshan as well as during festivals like Mahashivratri, when the temple is wonderfully decorated and filled with devotional energy. The premises are clean, well-organized, and easily accessible.

Whether you’re seeking spiritual comfort or just a quiet place to relax and reflect, Balrajeshwar Mandir offers a serene and uplifting experience. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Mulund! 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Govind Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Maa Ashapura Dham in Thane West is truly an oasis of calm amidst the city’s chaos. Located near Kapurbawdi Police Station on Majiwada Village Road, the temple may not be very visible from the main road, but once you enter, you are instantly surrounded by peace, positivity, and spiritual warmth.
The moment you step inside, you can feel strong divine energy and blessings all around. The temple is beautifully constructed, very clean, well-maintained, and filled with calming spiritual vibrations. The idol of Maa Ashapura is extremely powerful and graceful—just one darshan fills the heart with devotion, inner strength, and positivity.
The atmosphere during aarti is simply magical, with soulful chanting, ringing bells, and deep devotion everywhere. The priests and devotees are humble, welcoming, and respectful, making the experience even more comforting. Sitting here quietly for some time feels blissful, relaxing, and deeply meditative.
The temple complex is surrounded by several mini temples where you can also pray to Ganeshji, Hanumanji, Shivji, Krishna, Durga Maa, Santoshi Maa, Shitladevi, and more. There is another nearby temple close to the police station with idols of Ganeshji, Shivji, Dattatreya, and Maa Saptashringi, making this area spiritually very enriching. Shops are available both inside and outside the premises, and the Kapurbawdi Police Station is right beside the temple area, making it easy to locate.
Devotees strongly believe that Maa Ashapura fulfills wishes and protects her devotees. Many visitors feel a deep personal connection here, often describing it as a place for one-to-one spiritual conversation with Mataji. Attending the aarti and receiving bhandara prasad is a truly divine experience. You can even follow the temple’s Facebook page to watch live aarti.
Despite being close to one of the busiest traffic areas of Thane (Majiwada), the temple remains pristine, calm, and serene. It is a perfect place to spend quality time in silence, prayer, and reflection.
A must-visit spiritual destination for everyone in Thane and beyond.
🙏 Ashapura Mata Ki Jay! ✨

featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the most popular temple in Thane
Located at Majiwada Junction Thane
The Ashapura Devi Dham is located near Majiwada, in the district of Thane. This temple is 53 years old and was constructed in dedication to Goddess Ashapura. It is believed that the idol of Goddess Ashapura Devi is Swayambhu means it is created by itself and is not built by man. Tuesdays are usually crowded with many pilgrims visit to seek the Goddess blessings.
During Navratri people come here and decorations and hawan happens here
